text: Good. So now, looking back at C, we know that C uses the old standard IFS as, also in the previous example. But again, here things are a little bit different because it got a packet to transmit from inside layers earlier on. So how things are made here now is, C will have of course wait for the channel to become idle, and then use the extended IFS, and then draw the wakeoff image. So again, in the wakeoff procedure, BFS is now replaced with the extended IFS. Okay. At that point, we have done all nodes A, B, and C. All nodes A, B, and C have to draw the wakeoff values, and these wakeoff values as integers are nineteen for A, so very long. Thirteen, so even longer for B, while C draws five. Okay. So who is going to transmit first? Well, it's easy to see that the one that will decrease its wakeoff counter to zero first is C after five times lots, and that it will access the channel and transmit. All the other nodes will.
